environment.topology: 1 sync node (separate process) + embedded PostgreSQL 16 (control + 2 shards) + in-memory Redis stand-in; load generator on the same machine

config.editMix: insert 2 chars each; delete 1 char every 3rd edit
config.driver: maintainShard (the worker job): checkpoint, snapshot, verify, delete covered ops

caveats: Load generator and server run on the same machine and compete for CPU; the numbers are pessimistic for the server and say nothing about network latency.
One sync node only. Multi-node fan-out, reconnect storms and node-failure recovery need the Docker stack and are NOT measured here.
Redis is an in-process stand-in (ioredis-mock) and Postgres is an embedded build, so absolute throughput is not representative of managed services.
Propagation latency is measured between two sockets of the same load-generator process, so both sides share one clock.
